title: Count Perl word operators only in operator positions

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage report
Story: SEED-075#perl-word-operator-context; revision cb1ffa2270ba9cca9e103eeae6f2817515eb8b49 (closure tip eee5ff8c not used for the probe). Scratch: detached git worktree /tmp/lizard-intent-k7q (removed afterwards; execution checkout untouched).

Promise: the Svelte linear-time tests still catch a plausible quadratic regression in the Svelte markup scanner at the new `_LINEAR_TIME_SECONDS = 2` bound.

**VERDICT: Caught (limited to gross quadratic regressions).**
- Maintained assertion that caught it: test/test_languages/testSvelte.py::TestSvelteMarkup::test_many_divisions_in_interpolations_take_linear_time, line 671 `assertLess(time.perf_counter() - started, _LINEAR_TIME_SECONDS)`: "AssertionError: 174.44 not less than 2".
- Claim bounded to the path this test exercises (the per-interpolation `_MarkupTokens._code_end` read). I did not run the 7 other linear-time tests against the fault.

Baseline: `nix develop -c python -m pytest test/test_languages/testSvelte.py -q -k "linear_time or comment_starts"` gave 8 passed. The slowest tests ran 0.75s (divisions) and 0.68s (regexes). The others ran 0.27s or less.

Fault 1, used for the verdict. In lizard_languages/svelte.py `_MarkupTokens._code_end`, I changed `stop = self._guess(pos)` to `stop = end`. Each interpolation then tokenizes and mark-scans the rest of the markup instead of a bounded guess.
- Reach and wrong behavior: I checked with a scratch probe that reused the fixtures of the divisions, regexes and comment-starts tests at n = 50/100/200/400. Fixture results stayed correct, `[('f', 1, 1, 2)]`. The wrong behavior is only the time, and it grows quadratically.

| n | regex | divisions | comment starts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | 0.41s | 0.18s | 0.23s |
| 200 | 1.69s | 1.04s | 2.02s |
| 400 | 6.61s | 3.11s | 9.27s |

- Doubling n roughly quadruples the time. Extrapolated to the maintained n = 3000, the time is minutes. The divisions test took 174s.
- Under fault 1 the divisions test failed at 174s, and the 1s bound would have failed it identically. Only that one test was run under the fault.

Fault 2, discarded. In `_guess` I removed both `self.guess -= ...` budget decrements. All 8 linear-time/comment-start tests still passed, at 0.69s, 0.68s and 0.41s. I did not confirm that it reaches a path with unbalanced braces in the fixtures, so it is not evidence of an assertion gap. It is an unobserved reach, not a verdict.

Restoration: I restored the file from a copy. `git status` and `git diff` in the scratch checkout were clean, the same as the pre-probe state. The same command then gave 8 passed in 5.61s. I removed the scratch worktree and temp files.

Caveat for the 2s bound: the fixtures use n = 3000, so a gross quadratic with a realistic constant misses 2s by orders of magnitude. The promise is therefore supported for that class. A low-constant quadratic, or a regression only about 3x slower than the 0.7s baseline, could pass at 2s. Under the old 1s bound the margin was only about 1.4x, so the 2s bound does not meaningfully lose detection of gross regressions. I did not measure the borderline class.

**NEXT PROOF ACTION:** None required for the promise. The retrospective's "quadratic cases still miss 2s" claim is now verified for the divisions-fixture path under a full-rescan quadratic fault. Optional only: if the caller wants the borderline class covered, a scaling-based assertion (time at n versus 2n) would be a separate decision. This probe does not recommend it. No already-planned repair matches this evidence.

**COST ENTRIES**
- Test runtime: measured, pytest-reported. Baseline focused run 2.80s; fault-1 maintained test run 174.87s; restored rerun 5.61s. Scratch probe script runs (n up to 400) took about 38s wall, not pytest-reported. Fault-2 run 2.54s.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human time was observed or reported separately.
- Agent effort: unavailable. No token or tool-call count was exposed to me. As an estimate only, about 15 tool calls.
- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 661170 ms (measured), from 1795651070811 to 1795651731981 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: checked revision cb1ffa2270ba9cca9e103eeae6f2817515eb8b49; verdict Caught; no follow-up (next proof action none; the optional scaling-based assertion is not adopted and nothing is queued).
